newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen vows to seize resistance town.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen vows to seize resistance town.

text.p: Cambodian strongman Hun Sen said on Thursday he would immediately order his armed forces to seize the last town held by troops loyal to his ousted rival, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
"I will tell (armed forces chief) General Ke Kimyan to take over O'Smach by tomorrow," Second Prime Minister Hun Sen told reporters at Phnom Penh airport.
Hun Sen was returning from a meeting in Beijing with King Norodom Sihanouk who had asked Hun Sen and his delegation to pursue peace and national reconciliation in Cambodia.
O'Smach, a northwestern town on the border with Thailand, and a few small villages in the area, remain under the control of a ragged army loyal to Ranariddh, who was overthrown by Hun Sen on July 6.

Forces loyal to Hun Sen have been inching their way toward O'Smach and on Wednesday fired mortar rounds inside the town for the first time. Their advance has been hampered by booby traps and landmines laid by Ranariddh's retreating forces.
Truckloads of Thai troops armed with mortars and machine guns on Thursday reinforced the border to prevent any spill-over of fighting.
Some 15,000 refugees in the town were preparing to take refuge in Thailand and would be allowed to cross when the situation warranted it, Thai authorities said.
Hun Sen, who had Sihanouk in Beijing on Tuesday, said he expected that Ranariddh's forces would flee east to the Khmer Rouge stronghold of Anlong Veng when the government took O'Smach.
Hun Sen defended his July 6 power grab by claiming Ranariddh was conducting illegal negotiations with the Khmer Rouge and plotting to bring the rebels into the city to fortify his own forces.

Disagreement over policy towards the dwindling Khmer Rouge movement, architects of the 1975-1979 "killing fields" regime, drove a wedge between Hun Sen and Ranariddh, who shared power in an uneasy coalition government before the July 6 coup.
Ranariddh wanted to talk peace with rebels in Anlong Veng but Hun Sen called all negotiations with the outlawed rebels illegal.
Hun Sen said Ranariddh will be brought before a court if he returned to Cambodia to face charges of collusion with the rebels and illegal smuggling of weapons.
"When he arrives at the airport, he will be put in handcuffs," Hun Sen said on Thursday.
Sihanouk on Wednesday said he had asked Hun Sen to pursue peace, non-violence and national reconciliation in Cambodia and urged the powerful leader to respect human rights.
